mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate increase above 0.3 percentage points signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero in triggered months (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and monthly change < -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which increases risk premia and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both proxies exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates a broad-based collapse in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1% and HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 30% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals robust labor market expansion that supports consumer spending and corporate profitability, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both proxies meet the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of at least 0.4% for four consecutive months signals a manufacturing expansion that boosts earnings visibility and supports higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change >= 0.4% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in more than 70% of triggered periods.
